runs.question: How does the NIST Generative AI Profile describe data privacy risks?

answer.text:
The NIST Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) treats data privacy as one of its twelve GAI risks and defines it broadly. Its definition covers harms from personal information and sensitive data being exposed or misused. It defines Data Privacy as impacts from leakage and unauthorized use, disclosure, or de-anonymization of biometric, health, location, or other personally identifiable information or sensitive data.

The profile also explains what counts as sensitive. Per its footnote, what is categorized as sensitive data or sensitive PII can be highly contextual based on the nature of the information, but examples of sensitive information include information that relates to an information subject's most intimate sphere, including political opinions, sex life, or criminal convictions.

Data privacy is not placed in a single category. The profile sorts risks by origin and lists data privacy under three of them. Under technical or model risks it appears alongside Value Chain and Component Integration and Harmful Bias. Under misuse by humans it appears with CBRN Information or Capabilities and Information Security. Under ecosystem or societal risks it appears with Environmental impacts and Intellectual Property. The profile notes that some risks are cross-cutting between these categories.

The profile does not give a separate privacy-specific list of suggested actions in the pages I read. I could not run a keyword search because the search tool returned an error, so I read pages 5 through 8 directly. Later sections, including the suggested actions, may contain more privacy-specific guidance that I did not check.
